title: Two-zone oven heat-up with door interlock
nl_spec: A batch oven has two independently heated zones. Each zone heater is a simple thermostat: Heater1 is on while zone-1 temperature Temp1 is below its setpoint SET1 = 200 deg C, and Heater2 is on while zone-2 temperature Temp2 is below SET2 = 250 deg C (pure thresholds, no hysteresis). A shared door-interlock switch DoorClosed (TRUE = door closed) must gate ALL heating: whenever the door is open, both heaters are de-energized regardless of temperature, so an operator is never exposed to live heaters. Heating also requires the master Enable and a healthy emergency stop EStop, which is normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated). Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named oven_zones with inputs DoorClosed, Temp1, Temp2, Enable, EStop and outputs Heater1, Heater2.

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: When the door is open (DoorClosed = FALSE), both heaters are de-energized.
On emergency stop (EStop = FALSE), both heaters are de-energized.
Zone-1 heater is never on at or above its setpoint.
Zone-2 heater is never on at or above its setpoint.
Positive obligation: while healthy, enabled, door closed and zone-1 below setpoint, the zone-1 heater is on.
When the system is disabled (Enable = FALSE), both heaters are de-energized.

scenarios.description: Independent zone thermostats with door closed
Opening the door drops both heaters
Disable drops both heaters even with both zones below setpoint

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: access/door-interlocked multi-zone heating - a single shared interlock gates two independent process outputs. Uses pure thresholds (NO hysteresis, distinguishing it from a bang-bang controller and from the existing heater-overtemp task which is a latched trip). The door-open -> all-heaters-off obligation and the positive heat-demand obligation are the structurally novel property classes.
